newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Boliden sale seen most likely-newsletter.
newsitem.headline: Boliden sale seen most likely-newsletter.

text.p: Boliden, the mining unit of Swedish metals and rubber company Trelleborg, is more likely to be sold to another company than spun off as a separate unit, financial newsletter Borsveckan said on Monday.
Borsveckan said Boliden could be worth as much as all of Trelleborg is worth today when compared to other similar mining companies around the world.
In recent months the market has speculated that Trelleborg could be about to spin-off its Boliden unit.
Borsveckan said a sale seemed more likely than a separate listing on the bourse as Boliden had never really been commended by the market.
"Boliden was listed before Trelleborg bought it and it was never really a bourse success," Borsveckan said.
Even a totally free of debt Boliden would be unsexy, said Borsveckan.
Comparing Boliden with other mining companies, Borsveckan said Canada's Cominco was the best comparison.

"The most relevant presumption is to compare Boliden with Cominco -- both turn over around nine billion crowns. Similarly to Boliden ... zinc is the main metal for Cominco (48 percent)," the newsletter said.
"The company can in reality be worth as much as all of Trelleborg, around 12 billion crowns."
